title: The Tall Tower and Many Nations
bigQuestion: What happened at the tall tower, and how does the story say God planned to bless every nation?

story.title: The Block Tower
story.kicker: Three friends want to build the tallest tower ever. First they have to find a way to share.
paragraphs: It is block time in Room 12. Sofia, Ben and Amir want to build a tower. A tall one! They want it to touch the ceiling. They pull out every block in the bin.

But they cannot agree. Sofia wants only red blocks. Ben wants to build fast. Amir is still learning English. He tries to say an idea, but the others do not understand. Everyone talks at once. The tower wobbles. Then it falls down.
Their teacher, Ms. Lee, sits down with them. "What if you take turns?" she asks. "And what if you listen?" Amir shows them with his hands. He wants a wide bottom, so the tower will stand.
They try again. Each child adds one block. Then the next child adds one. Amir teaches them a word from his home language. The new tower is not the tallest. But it stands, and they built it together.
story.think: How did taking turns and listening help the three friends?

lessons.title: Let's Build a Tower!
lessons.mainIdea: Genesis 11 says people built a city and a tall tower to reach the sky.
reading: After the flood, Noah's family grew and grew. Genesis 11 says everyone spoke one *language*. They all used the same words.
The people found a flat land called Shinar. They made bricks and baked them hard. They said, let us build a city and a tall *tower*. Let its top reach the sky.
They wanted to make a big name for themselves. They did not want to spread out over the earth. But God had told people to fill the earth.

words.d: the words people use to talk to each other

look.title: Let Us Build
look.text: Come, let us make bricks. Let us build a city and a tower with its top in the sky. Let us make a name for ourselves, so we are not spread out over the whole earth.
look.cite: Genesis 11:3–4, paraphrased from the King James Version (1611)
look.prompt: What did the people want? Name two things.

check.q: How many languages did people speak at the start of Genesis 11?
check.why: Genesis 11 says everyone spoke one language.

check.q: What did the people want to build?
choices: A city and a tall tower
check.why: Genesis 11 says they wanted to build a city and a tower that reached the sky.

check.q: What did the people not want to do?
check.why: The people said they did not want to be spread out over the whole earth.

lessons.title: Mixed-Up Words
lessons.mainIdea: The story says God mixed up their language and spread the people over the earth.
reading: Genesis 11 says God came down to see the city and the tower. God saw what the people were doing.
Then, the story says, God mixed up their language. One person said a word. The next person did not understand it. They could not work together on the tower.
So the people stopped building. They had to *scatter* to many places. The city was called *Babel*. The name sounds like a Hebrew word that means to mix up.

words.d: the city in Genesis 11 where the story says languages got mixed up
to spread out in many directions

look.title: Say It Another Way
look.text: Try this. Say "hello" to a friend. Now think of other ways people say it. "Hola" in Spanish. "Bonjour" in French. "Ni hao" in Chinese. Same idea, different words.
look.prompt: Why was it hard for the people at Babel to keep building?

check.q: What did God do to the people's language, the story says?
check.why: Genesis 11 says God mixed up their language, so they could not understand each other.

check.q: What was the city called?
check.why: The city was called Babel. Shinar was the name of the flat land where it stood.

check.q: What happened after the language got mixed up?
choices: People moved away to many places
check.why: The story says the people stopped building and spread out to many places.

lessons.title: Families Become Nations
lessons.mainIdea: Families spread out and became many nations with many languages.
reading: Genesis 10 is a long list of names. It shows how Noah's family grew. Noah's sons were Shem, Ham and Japheth. Their children had children, and on and on.
Each big family became a *nation*. A nation is a large group of people. They share a land and often a language. Jewish tradition counts seventy nations in the list.
Today the world has about 7,000 languages. Some are spoken by millions of people. Some are spoken by only a few. Each one is a way to share ideas.

words.d: a large group of people who share a land and often a language

look.title: From One to Many
rows: Languages at the start of Genesis 11
look.cite: Genesis 10:1 and 11:1; the count of 70 is traditional
look.prompt: The story starts with one language. How many nations are in the list?

check.q: What were the names of Noah's three sons?
check.why: Genesis 10 says Noah's sons were Shem, Ham and Japheth.

check.q: What is a nation?
choices: A large group of people who share a land
check.why: A nation is a large group of people who share a land and often a language.

check.q: About how many languages are in the world today?
check.why: The world has about 7,000 languages today.

lessons.title: Heavenly Ones Over the Nations
lessons.mainIdea: Heiser read Deuteronomy 32 to say God put the nations under other heavenly ones for a time.
reading: *Deuteronomy* 32 is a song in the Bible. It tells how God split the people into nations. It says God gave each nation its own land.
Heiser studied very old copies of this song. One was found near the Dead Sea. It says God set the nations by the number of the *sons of God*. Many Bibles say sons of Israel there instead.
Heiser thought God let other heavenly ones watch over the nations for a time. But God kept one people for himself. Other readers think the verse is only about people.

words.d: the fifth book of the Bible
a Bible name that Heiser thought meant heavenly ones in God's family

look.title: The Song in Deuteronomy
look.text: When the Most High gave the nations their lands, he set their borders by the number of the sons of God. But the LORD kept his own people for himself.
look.cite: Deuteronomy 32:8–9, paraphrased from a Dead Sea Scroll reading; the King James Version (1611) has "children of Israel"
look.prompt: Whom does this song say God kept for himself?

check.q: What did Heiser think Deuteronomy 32 meant?
choices: God let heavenly ones watch over the nations for a time
God built the tower of Babel
check.why: Heiser read Deuteronomy 32 to say God let other heavenly ones watch over the nations for a time.

check.q: Where was one very old copy of this song found?
check.why: One very old copy of Deuteronomy 32 was found near the Dead Sea.

check.q: What do many Bibles say in this verse instead of sons of God?
check.why: Many Bibles, like the King James Version, say sons or children of Israel in this verse.

lessons.title: God Calls Abram
lessons.mainIdea: Right after Babel, Genesis tells how God chose one man, Abraham, to start a new family.
reading: Genesis 11 ends with a family from a city called Ur. One man in that family was Abram. Later God gave him a new name, *Abraham*.
In Genesis 12, God spoke to Abram. God said, leave your home and go to a new land. I will show it to you. Abram listened. He packed up and went.
Heiser noticed where this story sits. It comes right after Babel. He thought God was starting a new family there, one that would belong to God.

words.d: the man God called in Genesis 12; his first name was Abram

look.title: Abram Sets Out
rows: Genesis chapter where God calls Abram
Abram's age when he set out
look.cite: Genesis 11–12; Abram's age is from Genesis 12:4
look.prompt: How old was Abram when he set out? How close are the Babel chapter and the Abram chapter?

check.q: What was Abraham's first name?
check.why: Genesis says his first name was Abram. Later God gave him the name Abraham.

check.q: What did God tell Abram to do in Genesis 12?
choices: Leave home and go to a new land
check.why: In Genesis 12, God told Abram to leave his home and go to a new land.

check.q: What did Heiser notice about where Abram's story sits?
choices: It is the last story in the Bible
check.why: Heiser noticed that God calls Abram right after the Babel story.

lessons.title: A Blessing for Every Nation
lessons.mainIdea: Genesis 12:3 says all the families of the earth would be blessed through Abraham.
reading: God made Abram a big promise. Genesis 12 says God would make his family into a great nation. And more. Through him, all the families of the earth would be *blessed*.
To *bless* means to do good for someone. So the promise was not just for one family. It reached out to every nation, even the ones spread out at Babel.
Heiser thought this was God's plan to bring the nations back. Many Christians read it this way too. Jewish tradition honors Abraham as the father of the Jewish people.

look.title: A Promise for All Families
look.text: I will bless those who bless you. And in you, all the families of the earth will be blessed.
look.cite: Genesis 12:3, paraphrased from the King James Version (1611)
look.prompt: Who does this promise say will be blessed?

check.q: In Genesis 12:3, who would be blessed through Abram?
choices: All the families of the earth
check.why: Genesis 12:3 says all the families of the earth would be blessed through him.

check.q: What does it mean to bless someone?
check.why: To bless means to do good for someone.

check.q: What did Heiser think this promise was about?
choices: God's plan to bring the nations back
A plan to build the tower again
check.why: Heiser thought the promise to Abraham was God's plan to bring the nations back.

lessons.title: Taking Turns and Listening
lessons.mainIdea: Taking turns and listening help people work together.
reading: At Babel, the people wanted a big name for themselves. Then the story says their words got mixed up. They could not understand each other. The work stopped.
Working together takes care. It helps to *take turns*. It helps to *listen* all the way to the end. Then everyone gets a say.
Think of a class building a tower of blocks. One child adds a block. Then the next child does. Everyone waits. The tower grows, one turn at a time.

words.d: to let each person have a go, one after another

look.title: The Lunch Table
look.text: Look at the lunch table. Three friends want to tell a story at the same time. Nobody can hear. Then Kai says, "You go first." Each friend tells a story. Everyone laughs.
look.prompt: What helped the friends hear each other?

check.q: What does it mean to take turns?
choices: Let each person have a go, one after another
Only one person ever gets a go
check.why: Taking turns means each person has a go, one after another.

check.q: At Babel, what did the people want for themselves?
check.why: Genesis 11 says the people wanted to make a big name for themselves.

check.q: What helps a group work together?
check.why: Taking turns and listening all the way to the end help everyone get a say.

lessons.title: Kind to Every Language
lessons.mainIdea: People speak many languages. You can be kind to people who speak differently.
reading: In Chicago and all over Illinois, families speak many languages. You might hear Spanish, Polish, Arabic or Chinese on the bus. Each language comes from a family's story.
Someone may speak a language you do not know. You can still be *kind*. You can smile. You can point and show. You can learn one of their words.
The Babel story ends with people far apart. Abraham's story starts a promise to bless every nation. Being kind to people from every nation fits that promise well.

look.title: A New Friend
look.text: A new girl joins the class. She speaks Polish. She is still learning English. At recess she stands by the fence. Theo walks over. He smiles and holds out a ball.
look.prompt: What else could Theo do to help his new friend feel welcome?

check.q: What can you do if someone speaks a language you do not know?
choices: Smile and show them with your hands
check.why: You can smile, point and show. You can learn one of their words.

check.q: Which promise reached out to every nation?
choices: The plan to build a tower
The plan to build an ark
God's promise to Abraham in Genesis 12:3
check.why: Genesis 12:3 says all the families of the earth would be blessed through Abraham.

check.q: Which is a language many families speak in Chicago?
check.why: Many Chicago families speak Spanish. Babel is a city in the story, and Shinar is a land.

review.q: Which chapter of Genesis tells about the tall tower?
review.why: The tower story is in Genesis 11.

review.q: What was the city with the tower called?
Whom did God call to start a new family?
review.why: In Genesis 12, God called Abram, later named Abraham.

review.q: What did Heiser think Deuteronomy 32 says about the nations?
choices: They all spoke one language forever
God let heavenly ones watch over them for a time
They all lived on the ark
review.why: Heiser read Deuteronomy 32 to say God let other heavenly ones watch over the nations for a time.

choices: A tower that reaches the sky
All the families of the earth will be blessed
review.why: Genesis 12:3 says all the families of the earth would be blessed through Abraham.
Taking turns and listening help everyone get a say.
